title: Anomalous field evolution of the mixed-state linewidth in the second superconducting dome of LaFeAsO$_{1-x}M_x$ ($M={\rm F,H}$)
authors: Rustem Khasanov, Pierre Dalmas de Réotier, Samuele Sanna, Gianrico Lamura, Hubertus Luetkens, Matteo Moroni, Pietro Carretta, Rhea Kappenberger, Rowena Wachtel, Bernd Büchner, Sabine Wurmehl, Nikolai D. Zhigadlo
abstract: We report a transverse-field muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($μ$SR) study of the internal-field distribution in the mixed state of LaFeAsO$_{0.89}$F$_{0.11}$ and LaFeAsO$_{0.75}$H$_{0.25}$, representative of the first (SC1) and second (SC2) superconducting domes of the LaFeAsO$_{1-x}M_x$ ($M={\rm F,H}$) family, respectively. Below the superconducting transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, the linewidth of the internal-field distribution increases in both samples, indicating the formation of a vortex lattice. Above $T_{\rm c}$, the linewidth remains field dependent and increases approximately linearly with field, consistent with broadening of the powder spectrum caused by an anisotropic Knight shift. After subtraction of this normal-state contribution, the superconducting linewidth $σ_{\rm sc}$ exhibits qualitatively different field dependences in the two samples. At 4K, the SC1 ($x_{\rm F}=0.11$) sample shows the expected monotonic decrease with increasing field, whereas the SC2 ($x_{\rm H}=0.25$) sample develops a pronounced local maximum near 3T. A contour representation of $σ_{\rm sc}(T,H)$ further reveals a ridge of local maxima whose field position, $H_{σ,\max}(T)$, shifts to lower fields upon warming and disappears near $T_{\rm c}$. The anomalous field evolution observed in the SC2 sample is consistent with an additional field-induced contribution associated with enhanced Pauli-paramagnetic effects, highlighting the distinct electronic character of the two superconducting domes.
summary: This work uses muon-spin rotation ($\mu$SR) to compare the mixed-state linewidths of two superconducting domes in iron pnictides. The key finding is that while one dome (SC1) shows expected field behavior, the other (SC2) exhibits an anomalous local maximum. This anomaly points toward a distinct electronic mechanism in SC2, specifically enhanced Pauli-paramagnetic effects.
main_problem: The study investigates the anomalous field evolution of the mixed-state linewidth in two distinct superconducting domes (SC1 and SC2) within the $	ext{LaFeAsO}_{1-x}M_x$ family.
main_result: While SC1 shows conventional monotonic field dependence, SC2 exhibits a pronounced local maximum near 3 T at 4 K, suggesting an additional field-induced contribution from enhanced Pauli-paramagnetic effects absent in SC1.
method: Transverse-field muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements were used to probe the internal-field distribution in the mixed state of iron pnictides.
model_or_system: The system is based on layered iron-based superconductors, comparing $	ext{LaFeAsO}_{0.89}	ext{F}_{0.11}$ (SC1) and $	ext{LaFeAsO}_{0.75}	ext{H}_{0.25}$ (SC2). The analysis compares the superconducting linewidth ($\sigma_{sc}$) derived from $\mu$SR data.
key_observables: Mixed-state linewidth ($\sigma_{sc}(T, H)$), normal-state linewidth ($\sigma_n(H)$), and the field position of local maxima ($H_{\sigma,\max}(T)$).
important_parameters: Temperature (4 K), magnetic field (up to 8 T), doping concentrations ($x_{	ext{F}}=0.11$ vs $x_{	ext{H}}=0.25$).
main_assumptions: The anomalous behavior in SC2 is attributed to an additional field-induced contribution associated with enhanced Pauli-paramagnetic effects, which differs fundamentally from the physics governing SC1.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram of the superconducting domes and show temperature/field dependence plots ($\sigma(T)$ vs $H$) for both samples, highlighting the distinct low-temperature field behaviors.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes $\mu$SR data to compare SC1 and SC2. It first establishes the normal-state background, then isolates $\sigma_{sc}$. The core of the work compares the field dependence: monotonic decrease for SC1 versus nonmonotonic behavior with a local maximum for SC2.
why_interesting: The comparison between two distinct superconducting domes in the same material family provides an excellent platform to study how subtle changes in electronic structure (doping/substitution) can lead to fundamentally different magnetic responses, which is relevant to understanding complex many-body physics near quantum critical points.
